archetype.name: Rebuilding Year (offense arrived early)
archetype.definition: A rebuilding club whose young lineup jumped to the league's top three, while a thin bullpen and close-game losses kept the record at 77-85 even though the run differential was roughly break-even.

report.headline: Top-three offense, break-even run differential, 77 wins: the bullpen ate the difference.

recap.finish: 77-85, fourth in the NL East (17 games behind ATL); missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was the year Washington stopped being a doormat. After five straight seasons with a negative run differential, including -1.31 runs per game and 66 wins in 2025, the Nationals scored 821 runs and allowed 815. That works out to +0.04 per game, 15th in the league. The 11-win jump is real, and the underlying team was better than the record. A club with an even differential usually finishes around .500. Washington's W vs Run Diff of -4.5 ranked 25th, a near-exact reversal of the +4.5 that flattered last year's team.

The lineup drove the change. The offense ranked 3rd in runs per game with a .744 OPS, also 3rd, up from 20th and .693 a year ago. The park plays slightly hitter-friendly at 104, but the park-adjusted numbers say the gains are genuine. James Wood (142 wRC+, .388 OBP, 30 HR, 4.1 WAR) and CJ Abrams (124 wRC+, 33 HR, 34 SB, 3.7 WAR) were both All-Stars and both top-six at their positions on the site. Keibert Ruiz added a 105 wRC+ behind the plate. The lineup was top-heavy, though. Daylen Lile led the team in plate appearances with a 94 wRC+, and Dylan Crews sat at 82. Nasim Nuñez took 493 PA with a 53 wRC+ and a .244 slugging percentage, so his 49 steals came with almost no other offense.

Run prevention was the other half of the story, and it ranked 27th. The rotation (B-) had a genuine ace in Cade Cavalli: 3.02 ERA, 200 K, 28.3% strikeout rate, 3.9 WAR. Andrew Alvarez backed him with a 3.43 ERA and a matching 3.32 FIP. Behind them it thinned out. Jake Irvin posted a 5.48 ERA over 106.2 innings, and Connelly Early's 3.33 ERA sat on a 4.54 FIP. The bullpen graded D-, and it was the real leak. Miles Mikolas threw 116 relief innings with a 5.82 ERA, an 11.6% strikeout rate and -0.9 WAR. Closer Clayton Beeter collected 12 saves while walking 14.8% of hitters, with a 5.43 FIP. The defense didn't help either: -12 Fielding Runs, with Abrams alone at -13.8 at short.

The months show where it slipped away. A 12-15 April with a -21 run differential was the only month the team was clearly outplayed. A 16-12 May and a 13-14 June had them at 44-43 at the end of June. From there the record and the margin separated. July was 11-13 despite outscoring opponents by 14, and August went 11-18 while allowing only 4 more runs than they scored. That stretch, with a seven-game losing streak and no winning streak longer than four all year, is the signature of a bad bullpen and coin-flip games breaking the wrong way. A 33-42 finish over the last three months came with a near-even run differential.

They closed 6-4 and 11-11 in September and finished three games behind Miami for third. With 94 wins taking the division, a postseason push was never realistic. Still, this was the first Nationals team in the sheet's six-year window whose run differential was on the plus side.

highlights.title: Wood and Abrams lead a top-three offense
highlights.body: The offense went from 20th to 3rd in runs per game and from a .693 OPS to .744. Wood's 142 wRC+ and .388 OBP and Abrams' 33 homers and 34 steals were the engine, with both men top-six at their positions. This is driven by skill, not luck, and both are young enough that it should carry forward.

highlights.title: Cavalli pitches like an ace
highlights.body: Cavalli's 3.02 ERA was backed by a 3.25 FIP, a 28.3% strikeout rate and 200 strikeouts in 169.2 innings. That kind of underlying profile holds up. Alvarez's 3.43 ERA with a 3.32 FIP gives the rotation a believable second piece.

highlights.title: Run differential finally broke even
highlights.body: After -1.31 runs per game in 2025, the club finished at +0.04, 15th in the league. That roughly 1.35-run-per-game swing is the clearest measure of real improvement, and the record understates it.

lowlights.title: A D- bullpen that couldn't hold games
lowlights.body: Mikolas absorbed 116 relief innings at a 5.82 ERA while striking out only 11.6% of batters. Beeter closed while walking 14.8% of hitters, with a 5.43 FIP. With an offense this good, the bullpen is the most likely cause of the close-game losses. It needs the most work of any group.

lowlights.title: Record trailed the run differential
lowlights.body: A -4.5 W vs Run Diff ranked 25th. July (11-13 with a +14 margin) and August (11-18 with a -4 margin) cost the most. Much of this is close-game variance that tends to even out, but the bullpen made some of it worse.

lowlights.title: Lineup holes and leaky defense
lowlights.body: Nuñez's 53 wRC+ over 493 PA was a near-automatic out in the lineup. Crews (82) and Lile (94, a team-high 655 PA) were below average. The team gave back 12 Fielding Runs, with Abrams' -13.8 at shortstop the biggest share, which undercut a pitching staff already ranked 27th in runs allowed.

arc.note: The team recovered from a 12-15 April to sit at 44-43 at the end of June, then went 33-42 the rest of the way. That fade came even though the run differential over those three months stayed close to even.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is the lineup's core and the top of the rotation. Wood, Abrams and Cavalli produced 11.7 WAR between them, and their underlying numbers (wRC+, FIP, strikeout rate) back up the results. The -4.5 W vs Run Diff is the kind of thing that usually reverses, so this roster is closer to an 81-win team than its record shows. Getting past that needs a bullpen that isn't a D-: replacing Mikolas' innings and finding a closer who throws strikes are the clearest gains available. Upgrades at second base and in the corner outfield over Nuñez and Crews, plus better defense at short, are next. One caution: Early's 3.33 ERA ran well ahead of his 4.54 FIP, and Irvin's 5.48 shows the back of the rotation is not settled.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; run differential, luck and group grades all point the same way.
